# Confirm-ZbxProblem

## SYNOPSIS

Acknowledges problems, and adds a message, changes the severity, suppresses or closes them (event.acknowledge).

## SYNTAX

```
Confirm-ZbxProblem [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixProblem>[]> [-Message <string>] [-Severity <ZabbixSeverity>] [-Close] [-Suppress] [-SuppressUntil <DateTimeOffset>] [-Unsuppress] [-Unacknowledge] [-NoAcknowledge] [-CauseEventId <ulong>] [-ConvertToCause] [-PassThru] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Confirm-ZbxProblem cmdlet updates problems with event.acknowledge, the call behind the frontend's Update problem form. It acknowledges the problems given to -InputObject (event ids, problem names, or problems piped from Get-ZbxProblem; an event piped from Get-ZbxEvent binds by its EventId) and, in the same update, adds a -Message, changes the -Severity, suppresses them (-Suppress, or -SuppressUntil a time), ends a suppression (-Unsuppress), closes them (-Close, where the trigger allows manual close) or ranks them (-CauseEventId makes them symptoms of that problem, -ConvertToCause makes them causes again). -Unacknowledge removes the acknowledgement instead, and -NoAcknowledge makes only the other changes. Every problem the pipeline brings is updated in one call; the command writes the problems only with -PassThru, and -WhatIf shows what it would change. Pairs Zabbix refuses in one update (-Suppress with -Unsuppress, -Close with a suppression, -CauseEventId with -ConvertToCause) are refused before anything is sent.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Acknowledge a problem with a message

```powershell
Get-ZbxProblem -Host 'web-01' | Confirm-ZbxProblem -Message 'Looking into it' -PassThru | Select-Object Name, Severity, Acknowledged
```

Get-ZbxProblem writes the host's open problems; -PassThru writes them back, Acknowledged now True.

### Example 2: Hand a problem back

```powershell
Confirm-ZbxProblem -InputObject 'Too many requests on web-01' -Unacknowledge -Message 'Handing over to the night shift'
```

-Unacknowledge removes the acknowledgement; the message says why. -InputObject takes the problem's name.

### Example 3: Acknowledge every severe problem nobody has acknowledged yet

```powershell
Get-ZbxProblem -Group 'Web servers' -Severity High, Disaster |
    Where-Object { -not $_.Acknowledged } |
    Confirm-ZbxProblem -Message 'Seen by the on-call engineer'
```

A realistic morning check: -Severity keeps High and Disaster problems, Where-Object the unacknowledged ones.

### Example 4: Raise the severity and silence a problem for two hours

```powershell
Get-ZbxProblem -Host 'web-01' |
    Confirm-ZbxProblem -NoAcknowledge -Severity Disaster -SuppressUntil (Get-Date).AddHours(2) -PassThru |
    Select-Object Name, Severity
```

-NoAcknowledge leaves the acknowledgement as it is; -SuppressUntil takes a date and implies -Suppress. The server applies the suppression a moment later, so the problem's Suppressed turns True on its next read.

### Example 5: Close a problem once it is fixed

```powershell
Get-ZbxProblem -Host 'web-01' | Confirm-ZbxProblem -Close -Message 'Fixed: the service was restarted'
```

-Close needs a trigger that allows manual close (Set-ZbxTrigger -ManualClose); the server resolves the problem shortly after.

## INPUTS

- `ZabbixReference<ZabbixProblem>[]`: Bound to -InputObject (ByValue). Represents a reference to an API object: a parameter that points at an API object takes its id, its name, or the object itself piped from a Get- cmdlet, and becomes an id before the call — one parameter, three spellings, one resolution.

## OUTPUTS

- `ZabbixProblem`: The problem read model, as returned by the Zabbix API.
